items.name: Sawmill Gravy
items.hook: A milk gravy made in the pan with pork sausage or bacon drippings and flour, served over biscuits.

items.name: Sausage Gravy
items.hook: The national diner standard: crumbled pork breakfast sausage folded through a peppered milk gravy, served over biscuits.

items.name: Country (Cream) Gravy
items.hook: A white pan gravy made from the drippings of fried chicken, steak, or chops, with flour and milk or cream, seasoned hard with black pepper.

items.name: Red-Eye Gravy
items.hook: A thin, sharp gravy of country-ham drippings and black coffee, named for the circle of red fat that floats on it like an eye.

items.name: Chocolate Gravy
items.hook: A sweet breakfast gravy of cocoa, sugar, flour, and milk, cooked like a thin pudding and ladled over hot biscuits.

items.name: Tomato Gravy
items.hook: A roux-based gravy built on tomatoes, canned or fresh, with bacon fat or drippings.

items.name: Cornmeal Gravy
items.hook: An Appalachian gravy thickened with cornmeal instead of flour, giving a fine grain and a deep corn flavor.

items.name: Giblet Gravy
items.hook: The Thanksgiving gravy: turkey drippings and stock thickened with a roux, enriched with the chopped, simmered giblets — neck meat, heart, gizzard, liver — and often chopped egg.

items.name: Ham Gravy
items.hook: A thickened milk gravy built on baked-ham drippings and pan juices, the gravy of the holiday ham table.

items.name: Brown Gravy
items.hook: The all-purpose gravy: a browned roux loosened with beef, chicken, or mixed stock, dark and savory.

items.name: Onion Gravy
items.hook: A brown gravy built on slowly caramelized onions, sweet and deep.

items.name: Mushroom Gravy
items.hook: A gravy built on browned mushrooms and their liquor, roux-thickened with stock.

items.name: Chicken Gravy
items.hook: A pale, rich gravy from roast or fried chicken drippings and stock, flour-thickened.

items.name: Turkey Gravy
items.hook: Roast-turkey drippings and stock, flour-thickened and strained smooth.

items.name: Hamburger Gravy
items.hook: Ground beef browned and folded into a peppered milk or stock gravy: a mess-hall and school-cafeteria staple.

items.name: Liver Gravy
items.hook: The pan gravy made where liver was fried: drippings, flour, and water or milk, poured back over liver and caramelized onions.

items.name: Shrimp Gravy
items.hook: A Lowcountry gravy of shrimp, bacon or ham, peppers, and a light roux, made to pour over stone-ground grits.

items.name: Crawfish Gravy
items.hook: A Louisiana gravy of crawfish tails in a dark, peppery roux with the trinity of onion, celery, and bell pepper.

items.name: Chili Gravy (Tex-Mex)
items.hook: The defining sauce of Tex-Mex enchiladas: a smooth, brick-red gravy of stock, chili powder, and cumin, roux-thickened.

items.name: Bulldog Gravy
items.hook: A bare-bones camp gravy of flour, water or milk, and whatever grease the pan held, from the logging and mining camps.

items.name: Milk Gravy
items.hook: The plain form of the Southern white gravy: fat, flour, and milk, whisked smooth and peppered.

items.name: Pepper Gravy
items.hook: A cream gravy seasoned assertively with cracked black pepper, the Texas steakhouse form served over chicken-fried steak.

items.name: Bacon Gravy
items.hook: A milk gravy built purely on bacon drippings, flour whisked into the rendered fat, crumbled bacon folded back in.

items.name: Coffee Gravy
items.hook: A thin coffee gravy from the upland South: strong coffee stirred into pan drippings, sometimes lightly sweetened or thickened.

items.name: Sorghum Gravy
items.hook: A sweet breakfast sauce of sorghum syrup warmed with butter and a little water or cream, poured over biscuits and country ham.

items.name: Sunday Gravy
items.hook: The Italian-American Sunday sauce: tomatoes simmered for hours with braciole, meatballs, and sausage, called gravy in the Northeast's Italian-American kitchens.

items.name: Vegetarian Mushroom Gravy
items.hook: A meatless mushroom gravy built on vegetable stock and mushroom liquor, roux- or cornstarch-thickened.

items.name: Vegan Cashew Gravy
items.hook: A dairy-free white gravy of blended soaked cashews, water, and nutritional yeast, seasoned with black pepper and sage.

items.name: Gluten-Free (Cornstarch) Gravy
items.hook: Any gravy thickened with a cornstarch slurry instead of a wheat roux: glossy, clear-edged, and gluten-free.

items.name: Au Jus
items.hook: Roast-beef drippings served unthickened, 'with juice.' Documented here as the boundary case: it is served where gravy is served, but with no thickener it is a jus, not a gravy.

items.name: White Toast
items.hook: Plain toasted sandwich bread, the universal gravy base.

items.name: Texas Toast
items.hook: White bread cut twice as thick as standard, about an inch, griddled in butter.

items.name: Sourdough Toast
items.hook: Tangy, open-crumb toast from a levain loaf.

items.name: Whole Wheat Toast
items.hook: Toast from a whole-grain sandwich loaf: denser, nuttier, and sturdier than white.

items.name: Rye Toast
items.hook: Caraway-flecked rye bread, toasted.

items.name: English Muffin
items.hook: A fork-split, griddled muffin with a pocked interior made to catch gravy.

items.name: Buttermilk Biscuit
items.hook: The Southern buttermilk biscuit: tall, tender, and tangy, built to be split and gravied.

items.name: Split-Top Roll
items.hook: A soft white roll with a split baked into its top, the New England bakery roll.

items.name: Cornbread
items.hook: A wedge or square of skillet cornbread, split or crumbled as the base.

items.name: Grits
items.hook: Ground hominy corn cooked to a soft porridge, the Lowcountry's base.

items.name: Hash-Brown Base
items.hook: Shredded potatoes fried crisp on the griddle, used as a plated base.

items.name: Fried Mush
items.hook: Cooked cornmeal chilled firm, sliced, and fried crisp.

items.name: Johnnycake
items.hook: A cornmeal griddle cake of Rhode Island tradition, thin and crisp-edged.

items.name: Bagel
items.hook: A boiled-then-baked ring roll with a chewy crust, split and toasted.

items.name: Leftover Dressing Base
items.hook: Leftover baked dressing or stuffing, reheated crisp, used as a base for turkey and giblet gravy.

items.name: Creamed Chipped Beef on Toast (SOS)
items.hook: Creamed chipped beef on toast: dried beef folded into a white sauce over toast points.

items.name: Sausage Gravy over Biscuits
items.hook: The signature plate of the gravy world: split buttermilk biscuits under a full ladle of sausage gravy.

items.name: Chicken-Fried Steak with Cream Gravy
items.hook: A tenderized round steak, battered and fried like chicken, drowned in country cream or pepper gravy.

items.name: Open-Faced Hot Turkey
items.hook: Sliced roast turkey on bread, open-faced, covered in turkey gravy with mashed potatoes alongside.

items.name: Hot Beef Plate
items.hook: Sliced roast beef on bread with mashed potatoes, the whole plate flooded with brown gravy.

items.name: Country Ham with Red-Eye Gravy
items.hook: A thick slice of fried country ham with its red-eye gravy, biscuits on the side for sopping.

items.name: Biscuits with Chocolate Gravy
items.hook: Hot buttermilk biscuits split and covered in chocolate gravy, the sweet breakfast plate of the Ozarks and Appalachia.

items.name: Tomato Gravy over Grits
items.hook: A bowl of stone-ground grits under brick-red tomato gravy, the Lowcountry supper plate.

items.name: Shrimp Gravy over Grits
items.hook: Shrimp gravy spooned over stone-ground grits: the Lowcountry's defining plate, born a fishermen's breakfast and now its most famous export.

items.name: Hamburger Gravy over Toast
items.hook: Ground-beef gravy ladled over toast points: the cafeteria and farmhouse descendant of SOS, and a main-dish plate in its own right.

items.name: Fried Chicken with Cream Gravy
items.hook: Buttermilk fried chicken served with the cream gravy made from its own drippings.

items.name: Pork Chop with Sawmill Gravy
items.hook: A fried pork chop under sawmill gravy, the Appalachian farmhouse plate.

items.name: Liver and Onion Gravy Plate
items.hook: Floured liver slices fried and returned to their pan gravy with caramelized onions.

items.name: Crawfish Gravy over Cornbread
items.hook: Dark-roux crawfish gravy over a split wedge of skillet cornbread.

items.name: Eggs with Gravy (Diner Style)
items.hook: Fried or scrambled eggs served under sausage or milk gravy, diner style.

items.name: Scrapple with Gravy
items.hook: Crisp-fried scrapple slices with gravy, the Delaware diner plate.

items.name: Chicken-Fried Chicken
items.hook: A pounded chicken breast, battered and fried like chicken-fried steak, under cream or pepper gravy.

items.name: Smothered Pork Chops
items.hook: Pork chops browned, then braised in their own onion gravy until tender.

items.name: Smothered Steak
items.hook: Round steak braised tender in brown onion gravy.

items.name: Breakfast Stack
items.hook: Hash browns layered with eggs and sausage, flooded with sausage gravy.

pages.label: The Gravy Chart
pages.blurb: Every gravy on the site, one chart — bases, colors, and what they cover.

pages.label: Roux & lumps, solved
pages.blurb: Why gravy lumps, and how to never let it happen again.
